guidance.heading: Updated Business Outlook
section: The Company confirms that its revised guidance of total revenues and adjusted EBITDA provided in the second quarter of 2026 remains unchanged.
The Company now expects its capex for the full year of 2026 to be around RMB8,500 million, compared to RMB10,000 million of capex guidance provided in the second quarter of 2026.
This forecast reflects the Company’s preliminary view on the current business situation and market conditions, which are subject to change.

desk.headline: Revenue up 10.1% to RMB3.18bn, in line; profit slumps on last year's one-off gain; 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance kept, capex cut
results: Net revenue rose 10.1% to RMB3.18bn as data centres kept filling up; adjusted EBITDA grew a slower 2.8% to RMB1.38bn.
Margins narrowed: adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 43.4% from 46.5% and gross margin to 19.7% from 22.1%, mainly on higher utility costs.
Net income dropped to RMB28.5m from RMB728.6m, because last year included a gain from the C-REIT deconsolidation; diluted loss per ADS was RMB0.04.
Bookings were strong: 39,074 sqm of net new commitments, total committed area up 25.5%, and utilisation up to 81.2% from 74.4%.
Cash stood at RMB17.8bn against RMB9.3bn of short-term and RMB38.0bn of long-term debt; RMB2.3bn of new financing was raised in the quarter.

guidance.summary: GDS kept the full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance it revised in Q2 (the ranges are not restated in this release) and cut its 2026 capex plan to about RMB8.5bn from RMB10.0bn.

points: CEO William Huang pointed to strong new bookings while the company kept delivering its backlog.
He said customer move-ins were pushing utilisation higher.
CFO Dan Newman stressed the group's financial position and liquidity.
